This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,
examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary scalar vector magnitude direction component displacement velocity zero-vector opposite-vector free-vector >}}

## 2.1 Scalars and vectors

- A **scalar** has only a size: one number (health 75, time 42 s).
- A **vector** has a size (**magnitude**) and a **direction**.
- Distance is a scalar; **displacement** is a vector.
- Speed is a scalar; **velocity** is a vector.
- To move a car, the game needs the velocity: the speed alone does not say
  where the car goes.

![Scalar and vector.](images/scalar-vector.png){width=86%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Scalars and vectors in your game"}
Play a game for one minute. Write three scalars (for example "coins: 250") and
three vectors, each with a direction (for example "the ball flies up and to the
left").
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Scalar or vector?"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="both|neither"}
The score, 12 400.
:   scalar

"The player moves 3 units to the right in each frame."
:   vector

"The hit pushes the player 4 units away from the enemy."
:   vector

The waiting time of a skill, 2.5 s.
:   scalar

The game must move a car. Which does it need: the speed or the velocity?
:   the velocity
:::
:::

## 2.2 Arrows and components

- A vector is drawn as an **arrow**: length = magnitude, it points in the
  direction.
- A vector has **no position**: equal arrows anywhere are the same vector.
- The game stores the **components**: v = (v~x~, v~y~).
- Components = **head − tail**.
- The other way: head = tail + components.
- A negative component points the negative way: (0, 5) is straight up,
  (−2, 0) straight left.
- A joystick gives a vector every frame; let go → (0, 0), the **zero vector**.

![Components of the arrow from (1, 4) to (5, 1): (4, −3).](images/components.png){width=60%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Two enemies in different places that both move "2 left per frame" have the
**same** velocity vector.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Arrows in GeoGebra"}
At geogebra.org/calculator, type `u = Vector((1, 4), (5, 1))` and then
`w = Vector((4, -3))`. Read the components of both. Are they the same vector?
Why?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Arrows and components"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(−4, 3)|straight down"}
An arrow from (1, 4) to (5, 1). Components?
:   (4, −3)

An arrow from (−2, 3) to (4, −1). Components?
:   (6, −4)

The vector (3, −2) is drawn from (1, 4). Where is its head?
:   (4, 2)

The player lets go of the joystick. Which vector?
:   (0, 0)

Where does the vector (0, 5) point?
:   straight up
:::
:::

## 2.3 Points and displacement vectors

- A **point** is a place (where?). A **vector** is a change (how far, which way?).
- From A to B: **B − A** (end minus start).
- A − B is the **opposite vector**: same size, other direction.
- An arrow to the goal uses goal − player; a homing missile uses target − missile.
- On the goal, goal − player = (0, 0): no arrow to show.

![From the enemy E to the player P: P − E. The opposite, E − P, points back.](images/displacement.png){width=66%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"From A to B" is always B − A. An enemy that uses E − P walks **away** from
the player.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Chase the player"}
In GeoGebra, type your own points, for example `E = (-2, 1)` and `P = (3, 4)`.
Type `Vector(E, P)` and `Vector(P, E)`. Check the first one by hand with
P − E. Which vector does the enemy need?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Enemy, player, treasure"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(−8, 6)|it walks faster"}
Enemy E = (2, 7), player P = (6, 4). The vector from the enemy to the player?
:   (4, −3)

The vector from the player back to the enemy?
:   (−4, 3)

Player (−3, 2), treasure (5, −4). The arrow to the treasure?
:   (8, −6)

An enemy uses E − P instead of P − E. What happens?
:   it walks away from the player

The player stands on the goal. Goal − player?
:   the zero vector
:::
:::

## 2.4 Moving a point with a vector

- point − point = vector; point + vector = point; point + point = no meaning.
- **Velocity**: the displacement in one frame.
- Every frame: new position = old position + velocity.
- After n frames: n × v~x~ along x and n × v~y~ along y.
- Reverse question: velocity = total displacement ÷ number of frames.
- The opposite velocity brings an object back to its start.

![Five frames with v = (2, 1) per frame.](images/per-frame.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/vector-dash.html" poster="sims/vector-dash.png" title="Vector Dash: one velocity, n frames" kind="game" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Vector Dash"}
Play three levels of **Vector Dash**. For one level, write the start, the
target, the number of frames and your velocity. Check it: total displacement ÷
frames.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Frame by frame"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(8, 4)|after 3 frames|a vector"}
A ship at (1, 1) with velocity (2, 1). Where after 4 frames?
:   (9, 5)

A missile at (10, 7) must reach (4, 1) in 3 frames. Velocity?
:   (−2, −2)

A ball at (12, 3) with velocity (−3, 1). When is x = 0?
:   after 4 frames

A platform at (2, 5) moves with (2, 0) for 3 frames. Where is it?
:   (8, 5)

What is point + point?
:   no meaning

An object has the velocity (0, 0). What does it do?
:   it stands still
:::
:::

## 2.5 Vectors in three dimensions

- A 3D vector has three components: (v~x~, v~y~, v~z~).
- Displacement is still end − start, one component at a time.
- y up: **vertical** part (0, v~y~, 0) changes the height.
- **Horizontal** part (v~x~, 0, v~z~) moves along the ground.
- Walking on flat ground: v~y~ = 0. A jump changes only v~y~.

![A drone flight split into a horizontal and a vertical part.](images/drone-3d.png){width=70%}

{{< sim file="sims/position-3d.html" poster="images/axes-3d.png" title="Move the player in 3D" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A 3D move"}
In the 3D viewer, put the player at (1, 0, 1), then move it to (4, 3, 5).
Write the displacement, its vertical part and its horizontal part.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · A drone in 3D"}
A drone flies from A = (2, 0, 1) to B = (6, 5, −3). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(4, 0, 0)|5"}
The displacement from A to B.
:   (4, 5, −4)

Its vertical part.
:   (0, 5, 0)

Its horizontal part.
:   (4, 0, −4)

The way back, from B to A.
:   (−4, −5, 4)

A character walks on flat ground. Its v~y~ is…
:   0
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Comet Courier {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

![The star map of Comet Courier.](images/comet-courier.png){width=88%}

**Comet Courier** is a delivery game in space. Depot Alpha is at (1, 2),
depot Beta at (9, 6), and a comet passes through (5, 4). The player chooses
one velocity before the ship starts; the game adds it once per frame. If the
ship passes through the comet's point, it is hit. In 3D, station Gamma is at
(2, 1, 3) and station Delta at (6, 4, 3).

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Alpha to Beta (harder)"}
Use the numbers of Comet Courier. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(4, 4)|after 3 frames|(0, 0, 3)"}
The displacement from Alpha to Beta.
:   (8, 4)

A ship leaves Alpha with (2, 1). After how many frames is it at Beta?
:   4 frames

Is that ship hit by the comet? When?
:   yes, after 2 frames

The velocity to reach Beta from Alpha in only 2 frames.
:   (4, 2)

The displacement from Gamma to Delta.
:   (4, 3, 0)

The vertical part of that move.
:   (0, 3, 0)
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- A scalar is one number; a vector has a size and a direction.
- Components = head − tail; a vector has no position.
- From A to B: B − A; A − B is the opposite vector.
- Every frame: position + velocity; velocity = displacement ÷ frames.
- 3D: three components; vertical part (height) and horizontal part (ground).
